topics.topic: Identity and reuse of AdmissionVerdict across repeated admissions
questions: When the same implementation is admitted again over the unchanged corpus, is the result the existing AdmissionVerdict, a new verdict entity, or a new value distinguished by its new execution evidence?
When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a new verdict created for the newly minted TrialExecutions and decided_at?

When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus, is a new AdmissionVerdict created for the new TrialExecutions and `decided_at`, or is the existing verdict reused despite the required rerun?

judgement.why: The topic repeats P1, and the change touched only the State 0 secrets passage.

precedent.topic: AdmissionVerdict identity for repeated submission against an unchanged corpus
quotes: Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.
precedent.why: The later rule says the existing verdict is reused, so no new admission TrialExecutions are created for an unchanged implementation-and-corpus pair.

topics.topic: Whether NodeExecution is an occurrence entity or a substitutable value, and how it is identified
questions: Is a NodeExecution an entity representing one particular attempt, identified by its attempt coordinates, or a substitutable value identified by all of its facts?
Is NodeExecution a content-derived value or an occurrence entity identified by run_id, node_id, map_index and attempt_number?
Is NodeExecution a value or an issued entity observation, and what exact facts mint or identify it?

judgement.why: The topic repeats P6, and neither identity passage changed.

quotes:
### Identity

value

### Identity evidence

Substitution: an attempt's record is issued once. Continuity: none; a further
attempt is a further record.

Substitution: fails — an execution is an observation; two runs of the same pair
are two observations with equal facts possible, and both are kept, so the
record is told apart by its minted `trial_execution_id` (A01 rule 2), not by its
values. Continuity: trivial; it is issued once and never changed. Entity issued
once, not a value (SPEC_STANDARD 15.1.1: a value has no identifier of its own;
pre-contract data closure, 2026-10-03).
precedent.why: The change did not touch either identity passage or make NodeExecution identity newly consequential.

topics.topic: Effect of trial-corpus growth on existing activations
questions: After a new TrialCase is added, what happens to an implementation activated under the previous corpus?
What happens to an existing activation when a trial case is added and its implementation has no admitted verdict over the enlarged current corpus?

judgement.why: The topic repeats P2, and the change did not affect trial corpora or activations.

quotes:
Capturing a failed execution (M06 rule, State 0 action) adds a case and so
   changes the corpus digest; the serving implementation keeps serving. It
   visibly lacks a verdict over the current corpus when the slot is inspected,
   and serves until another implementation is activated.

A run starts from the flow's active version. Before any node executes, the
   kernel checks, in this order, and refuses the start without creating a run on
   the first that fails: the flow exists and has an active version; the request
   supplies exactly the flow's input ports; each value, in port name order, fits
   its port's schema and then its size bound —
   for a `many` port, is a JSON array whose every element fits it — and
   is within `stored_value_bytes_max`; every function node's contract version has
   a current activation.
precedent.why: State 2 says corpus growth leaves the existing implementation serving, and run start requires a current activation rather than a current-corpus verdict.

topics.topic: How a Run retains the exact FlowActivation used as later draft-write authority
questions: How does a Run identify the exact FlowActivation whose owner authority a later draft-write EffectAttempt must record, especially if the same version is activated more than once?
How does a Run retain the exact FlowActivation identity needed later as a draft-write EffectAttempt's authority, especially when the same version can be activated more than once?

quotes:
3. **Which FlowActivation a `draft-write` send names** (A10 rule 6): the latest
   FlowActivation of the run's pinned version before the Run record in store
   order — the one under which it started. `runs` finds it and passes it to
   `effects` with every call about one of the run's elements (State 3, "Facts
   passed down"); store order, not time, so two records never tie. A run's
   version was active when it started (A12 rule 1), so "none" cannot occur;
   if it does, the store is inconsistent and the call is `internal_error`.
judgement.why: The later public-API text specifies how the exact FlowActivation is recovered and passed to effects.

topics.topic: Identity of ProofResult when proof status changes for the same flow version
questions: What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can be unproven before a binding is accepted and proven afterward?
What identifies a ProofResult when the same immutable flow version can first be unproven and later proven after a referenced binding changes from proposed to accepted?

judgement.why: The topic repeats P3, and neither the ProofResult passage nor the binding-state issue changed.

precedent.topic: ProofResult identity when binding status changes
quotes: Substitution: proving the same version gives the same result. Continuity: none.
precedent.why: The change did not touch M17 or make ProofResult identity newly consequential.

topics.topic: MCP operations exposing primary actions absent from the fixed operation set
questions: Which MCP operations expose each primary action omitted from K-11's stated fixed set?

How are the primary actions to add or capture a trial case, release a failed run, roll back a slot, propose a binding, compose and prove a flow, and refuse an effect exposed, given that they are absent from the stated fixed MCP operation set?

quotes:
The one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp` (K-11), one per State 0
action. Each is handled by `module:surface` in A16 rule 1 order and then calls
the module operation named; every answer is masked for an agent under A07
rules 4–5. Field schemas and bounds are State 6's. "Agent" means any agent,
"author" an agent with the author right.

| `add_trial_case` | author | `functions.add_trial_case` |
| `submit_implementation` | author | `functions.submit_implementation` |
| `try_implementation` | agent | `functions.try_implementation` |
| `capture_failed_execution` | owner, author | `runs.capture_failed_execution` |
| `roll_back_slot` | owner, author | `functions.roll_back_slot` |
| `propose_binding` | agent | `bindings.propose_binding` |
| `accept_binding` | owner | `bindings.accept_binding` |
| `compose_flow_version` | agent | `flows.compose_flow_version` |
| `prove_flow_version` | agent | `flows.prove_flow_version` |
| `activate_flow_version` | owner, agent (`read` only, A06) | `flows.activate_flow_version` |
| `start_run` | owner, agent | `runs.start_run` |
| `resume_run` | owner, agent | `runs.resume_run` |
| `release_run` | owner, agent | `runs.release_run` |
| `decide_effect_approval` | owner | `runs.continue_after_approval` |
judgement.why: The later MCP catalogue names the operation exposing every questioned action, including approval or refusal through `decide_effect_approval`.

topics.topic: Whether an unsuccessful execution can be captured after completion and spool removal
questions: Can a failed function execution be captured after its run ended `refused` or `cancelled`, especially when its inputs included spooled files whose bytes have already been removed?
Can an unsuccessful function execution be captured after its run ended `refused`, `cancelled`, or `succeeded`, given that such a run was not released but its file spool has already been removed?

quotes:
5. Capturing a failed execution into a trial corpus (M06) is allowed only for
   a function node's execution that ran in the sandbox — its record names the
   resources it used — and did not succeed; a node that concluded without
   running, a receiving node refusing a misfit input among them, is not
   captured. It is allowed only while
   its run still holds its spool — the run has not ended, or ended `failed` and
   was not released — and is refused otherwise, since its files may be gone.
judgement.why: The later run rule permits capture only before the run ends or from an unreleased failed run, so capture after succeeded, refused or cancelled is refused.
